answer: DeepWalk works well in the 3% labeled Flickr setting because it first learns low-dimensional node embeddings from the graph’s random walks, so nodes that are structurally or locally close end up near each other in embedding space even without labels. SpectralClustering then groups these embeddings into communities that reflect the graph’s latent structure, which is especially helpful on Flickr because the network is highly homophilous and community-like. As a result, the method can exploit the large amount of unlabeled graph structure to propagate information from the small labeled subset, while many baselines rely more directly on the scarce labels or weaker feature assumptions. That combination lets DeepWalk capture useful global and local connectivity patterns and generalize better than the baselines under extreme label scarcity.
